questions.stem: A bronze column order_ts holds timestamps as strings. How should silver standardize it?

options.text: Cast it with to_timestamp (or CAST AS TIMESTAMP) into a timestamp column
Convert it to an integer of characters

questions.explanation: to_timestamp parses a string into a timestamp; silver standardizes types so queries compare and filter correctly.

questions.stem: Rows with a null order_id can't be used. Which SQL keeps only usable rows for silver?

options.text: SELECT * FROM bronze_orders WHERE order_id != NULL
SELECT * FROM bronze_orders WHERE order_id = NULL
SELECT * FROM bronze_orders WHERE order_id IS NOT NULL

questions.explanation: A comparison with NULL returns NULL (unknown), not true, so WHERE drops it; use IS NOT NULL.

questions.stem: Why do silver tables read from bronze rather than from the source again?

options.text: Bronze keeps the raw history, so silver can be rebuilt or corrected without going back to the source
Bronze is faster than any source

questions.explanation: Keeping raw data in bronze lets you reprocess silver with new rules without re-ingesting.
